t: You are standing in Leicester Square, where for a few years in the Victorian era there was an attraction called Wyld's Great Globe. It stood here between 1851 and 1862, and nothing of it remains. It was built by James Wyld, a mapmaker and geographical publisher who had also been a Member of Parliament for Bodmin. He is best remembered for this globe, which put his trade as a map-seller on public display in the middle of London.
